A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FLARE study. All 22 pages of v3 and 19 pages of v5, including appendices, are readable, and corresponding methods, results, figures, and tables can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations in Tables 1–2, a plan-only ablation, and empirical analyses of search traces, faithfulness, and model scale.

after.justification: v5 retains original benchmark and diagnostic results and adds GPT-4o evaluations and code self-refinement results in Table 2.

M1.justification: v5 introduces FLARE_SR=2, adding up to two code self-refinement iterations (Section 5.1 and Table 2). The underlying plan, code, simulated-search, and answer-generation pipeline and its prompts remain intact.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine math, multi-hop QA, and relational-inference datasets, plus PrOntoQA, LogicalDeduction, and AR-LSAT. The additional backbone and refinement experiments use retained task coverage.

E2.justification: The QA comparators remain CoT and F-CoT; the logic comparators remain Standard prompting, CoT, and Logic-LM. GPT-4o is an added backbone, while self-refinement is a FLARE variant rather than a new external baseline.

E3.justification: Table 2 extends evaluation to GPT-4o and adds a maximum-two-iteration refinement condition. The documented dataset sample counts and few-shot counts remain unchanged. v5 removes explicit greedy-decoding prose, but Algorithm 1 retains argmax, leaving any actual decoding change unresolved.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds a comparison testing the effect of code self-refinement. Section 3.3 also newly reports that other, unspecified string-matching techniques yield the same trends, without detailed supporting results. Existing plan-only, search-trace, and scale analyses are retained, with the scale analysis moved to Appendix A.1.

E5.justification: The boxplots and error bars in Figures 2–4 retain their reporting practices. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and v5 introduces no confidence-interval definitions, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises all nine Llama-3.1-8B CoT scores, including GSM8K from 59.2 to 85.2 and Date from 20.9 to 74.1, changing several within-model rankings. GPT-3.5 FLARE's GSM8K score changes from 68.1 to 82.1. Table 2 adds GPT-4o and self-refinement results; GPT-4o FLARE_SR=2 reports 99.24, 90.33, and 45.02 on the three logic tasks. These are revised or newly reported results, not established cross-version performance gains under verified identical settings.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4) remove argmax from the conditional-generation expressions, making a limited revision to the mathematical specification. Algorithm 1 still uses argmax, leaving the intended decoding rule inconsistent. The fact/relation conditions, faithfulness construction, and absence of theoretical proofs are otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: v5's abstract adds a claim of best performance on all three logic benchmarks, extending v3's introductory claim of two out of three through the new refinement results. The introduction explicitly focuses on models not trained on reasoning traces. The seven-of-nine QA claim and central faithfulness contributions remain.

C2.justification: New Limitations text identifies propagation of formalization errors, dependence on prompt following, prompt sensitivity, and incomplete exploration of large or open-ended spaces. The new impact discussion also explains how convincing formalization can conceal flawed premises or biases. Existing interpretations of faithfulness and search behavior largely remain.

D1.justification: v5 removes v3's Reproducibility Report, including its statements about releasing code, processing pipelines, prompts, and model outputs, and fixing temperature for greedy decoding. Appendix prompts, dataset statistics, and pseudocode remain. This removes documentation; it does not establish that resources were withdrawn.

R1.justification: v5 adds Chen et al. (2024), Wang et al. (2025), and Zhang et al. (2025) to motivate its focus away from reasoning-trace-trained models. It removes the Gehrmann, Reif, and Sanh citations from the condensed natural-language reasoning discussion. The broader positioning against prompting and external symbolic solvers remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, related-work discussion, and dataset descriptions are substantially condensed and rewritten. The Prolog rationale and scale analysis move into the appendix, contribution bullets become inline enumeration, and limitations, impact, and acknowledgments sections replace the earlier ending structure containing the reproducibility report.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. Table 2 expands into backbone groups with refinement columns; Tables 4–5 become side-by-side displays, and Table 5 adds aggregate rows. Figures 3–4 move to the appendix, with Figure 3's retained panels stacked and its legends repositioned. Appendix tables and the code example are also reformatted.

improvement.justification: The added GPT-4o/refinement comparisons and explicit limitations provide useful evidence and qualifications. However, v5 changes GPT-3.5 FLARE's GSM8K score to 82.1 in Table 1 while retaining 68.1 in Table 3 without explaining a setting difference, removes reproducibility disclosures, and leaves generation equations inconsistent with Algorithm 1. These benefits and reporting regressions prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
